mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.25% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.25% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS changes (p > 0.05 in OLS regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: Multivariate Granger causality test rejects PAYEMS leading UNRATE in predicting SPX 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 suggests weakening manufacturing demand, which tends to depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers above 105 within 2 months without a corresponding SPX negative return (correlation < -0.3).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) to personal consumption expenditures (not available in proxies) suggests accelerating inflation, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days tend to be negative due to investor anticipation of rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate exceeds 0.3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns remain positive despite CPIAUCSL accelerating inflation (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the 2-year Treasury yield (not directly observable but proxy via FEDFUNDS behavior) combined with rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) creates a risk of rate hikes, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls below 1.5% while CPIAUCSL monthly increase exceeds 0.4% in the same month
failure_condition: No significant negative return in 60 days when both triggers are met (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in housing starts (not available - use HOUST as proxy for housing activity) and a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) jointly indicate economic expansion, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 2% month-over-month and UNRATE falls by > 0.1 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when both indicators are in expansion phase.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days are typically negative due to expected market volatility and profit-taking.
regime_hint: any regime during FEDFUNDS rising trend
failure_condition: More than 60% of 5-day forward returns are positive when FEDFUNDS is in an upward trend (contrary to expectation).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of monthly retail sales (not available - use PAYEMS as proxy for consumer demand) to industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 0.8, it indicates a demand-supply imbalance favoring supply, which tends to push S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS / INDPRO < 0.8 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns remain positive despite sustained supply-side imbalance (p < 0.05 in regression).
